title: Windows, PowerShell & VS Code Operations Core v2

domain.name: Windows, PowerShell & VS Code Operations
domain.description: Advanced Windows and PowerShell operations covering modules, robust automation, networking diagnostics, services, scheduled work, editor automation, environment recovery, and controlled incident response. Version-sensitive OS/tool behavior belongs in Current Intelligence.

competencies.name: Advanced PowerShell Functions & Modules
competencies.description: Build reusable advanced functions, parameter contracts, modules, structured output, and testable automation.
competencies.purpose: Turn one-off shell commands into maintainable operational tools.

units.title: A script becomes reliable when its interface is explicit
units.content: Inputs, output objects, errors, side effects, required privileges, and supported environments should be part of the function contract.

units.title: Module design workflow
units.content: Define command responsibility, parameters and validation, structured output, terminating-error policy, internal helper boundaries, module exports, help examples, and tests before broad reuse.

units.title: Module failure modes
units.content: Avoid global mutable state, output mixed with display formatting, silent error swallowing, aliases in production code, and modules that modify machine state merely on import.

drills.title: Design a reusable FREEOS operations module
drills.prompt: Specify a PowerShell module for status checks, path validation, process inspection, and safe previewed maintenance actions.

competencies.name: Robust Errors, Logging & Idempotence
competencies.description: Build automation that fails predictably, records evidence, supports reruns, and verifies postconditions.
competencies.purpose: Make repetitive system operations safer and diagnosable.

units.title: Failure behavior is part of automation design
units.content: A script must define what stops the run, what can be retried, what state may already have changed, and how a rerun behaves.

units.title: Reliable automation pattern
units.content: Validate prerequisites, emit structured logs, use try/catch/finally intentionally, make changes idempotently, verify each postcondition, persist enough state for recovery, and stop on unsafe ambiguity.

units.title: Reliability failures
units.content: Avoid continue-on-error defaults, reruns that duplicate changes, logs containing secrets, cleanup that destroys first-failure evidence, and success messages before postcondition checks.

drills.title: Harden a maintenance script
drills.prompt: Redesign a script that edits PATH, moves caches, and restarts services so reruns and partial failures are safe.

competencies.name: Networking, DNS & Port Diagnostics
competencies.description: Diagnose localhost, LAN, DNS, routes, listeners, firewall boundaries, and application reachability methodically.
competencies.purpose: Separate name-resolution, transport, binding, and application failures.

units.title: Reachability has layers
units.content: A hostname can resolve while the route fails; a port can listen while firewall or binding scope blocks access; an HTTP service can respond while the application itself is unhealthy.

units.title: Connectivity isolation workflow
units.content: Capture target host and expected port, resolve names, inspect local bindings and owning processes, test route/connectivity, compare loopback versus interface access, inspect firewall policy without changing it first, then test application protocol.

units.title: Network diagnostic failures
units.content: Avoid disabling firewall broadly to test one port, assuming ping proves application reachability, editing DNS before checking bindings, and killing an owning process without identifying it.

drills.title: Diagnose a remote dashboard connectivity issue
drills.prompt: Build an isolation sequence for a dashboard reachable locally but not through a private network interface.

competencies.name: Windows Services & Scheduled Operations
competencies.description: Inspect, configure, and troubleshoot services and scheduled tasks with privilege, startup, dependency, and failure awareness.
competencies.purpose: Run persistent local systems without unsafe blanket elevation.

units.title: Background execution changes identity and environment
units.content: Services and scheduled tasks may run under different users, working directories, environment variables, privileges, and desktop sessions than interactive terminals.

units.title: Background-task workflow
units.content: Define execution identity, working directory, command, environment, trigger, restart/failure policy, log path, and least privilege; test manually under equivalent context before enabling automatic execution.

units.title: Background-operation failures
units.content: Avoid storing credentials in task arguments, relying on mapped drives unavailable to service accounts, enabling auto-restart loops with no backoff, and running whole toolchains as administrator unnecessarily.

drills.title: Design a safe FREEOS startup task
drills.prompt: Specify how a local FREEOS service could start reliably after login or boot while preserving logs and least privilege.

competencies.name: VS Code Debug, Tasks & Workspace Automation
competencies.description: Create repeatable launch, task, problem-matcher, multi-root, and debugging workflows for complex projects.
competencies.purpose: Turn VS Code into a reproducible operator console instead of a machine-specific setup.

units.title: Editor automation should encode project workflow
units.content: Build, test, debug, lint, logs, and common maintenance tasks can be repository-defined when they avoid secrets and machine-specific assumptions.

units.title: Workspace automation workflow
units.content: Define canonical commands, add tasks with explicit cwd, add debug configurations for real entry points, use problem matchers where useful, separate user-specific settings, and document required extensions without auto-trusting third-party code.

units.title: Workspace automation failures
units.content: Avoid absolute user paths in committed settings, hidden environment assumptions, tasks that mutate production by default, and globally changing editor settings to fix one repository.

drills.title: Build a production FREEOS VS Code workspace plan
drills.prompt: Design tasks and debug launchers for API, dashboard, tests, logs, and Remote Ops.

competencies.name: Environment Recovery & Package Managers
competencies.description: Recover broken Node, Python, Conda, package-manager, PATH, and native dependency environments with minimal collateral change.
competencies.purpose: Repair toolchains without reinstalling the whole machine blindly.

units.title: Environment identity must be proven before repair
units.content: Executable resolution, active environment, package location, lockfiles, runtime architecture, and process PATH may differ even on the same machine.

units.title: Environment recovery workflow
units.content: Capture versions and executable paths, reproduce in a clean shell, inspect lockfiles/environment manifests, verify one runtime at a time, repair the smallest scope, then re-run the original failing command.

units.title: Environment recovery failures
units.content: Avoid deleting environments before exporting manifests, globally installing packages to solve local conflicts, mixing package managers without ownership rules, and editing system PATH without proving resolution order.

drills.title: Recover a mixed runtime failure
drills.prompt: Create an isolation plan when Node works in one shell, Python/Conda in another, and a GPU package fails only inside one environment.

competencies.name: Incident Recovery & Change Control
competencies.description: Respond to local system failures using evidence capture, safe containment, controlled changes, rollback, and post-incident notes.
competencies.purpose: Restore service without making the system harder to understand afterward.

units.title: Recovery and diagnosis compete for evidence
units.content: Emergency changes can destroy logs, timestamps, and state needed to identify root cause; capture first-failure evidence before broad remediation when safe.

units.title: Incident workflow
units.content: Record symptom and time, preserve logs/config/status, define affected scope, choose reversible containment, change one thing at a time, verify recovery, then document root cause confidence and follow-up prevention.

units.title: Incident-response failures
units.content: Avoid reboot-first habits for every issue, disabling security controls broadly, deleting logs/caches before preserving evidence, and declaring root cause from correlation alone.

drills.title: Run a local service incident review
drills.prompt: FREEOS becomes unreachable remotely while local processes still appear active. Build a recovery and evidence plan.

competencies.name: Controlled Remoting, Jobs & Parallel Work
competencies.description: Understand PowerShell jobs, background work, remoting concepts, serialization boundaries, and safe concurrency.
competencies.purpose: Run longer operations without losing scope, output, or control.

units.title: Remote and background sessions have different state
units.content: Variables, credentials, modules, filesystem paths, environment, and object serialization may differ from the interactive session that launched the work.

units.title: Background-work workflow
units.content: Define exact target and command, pass only required inputs, log output and errors, bound concurrency, collect results, verify completion, and keep remote authentication/configuration outside scripts when possible.

units.title: Remoting and job failures
units.content: Avoid embedding secrets, unbounded fan-out, assuming local drive mappings exist remotely, abandoning failed jobs without logs, and enabling broad remote administration merely for convenience.

drills.title: Design a bounded parallel inspection job
drills.prompt: Plan a PowerShell workflow that checks several local project folders or services in parallel without changing state.
